restatements.text: Prohibits county jails from holding individuals past their scheduled release time based solely on a federal immigration detainer.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released
evidence.why: It establishes a single statewide rule, removing the ability of individual counties to set their own policies on immigration holds.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request
evidence.why: It strengthens legal protections for incarcerated individuals by ensuring they are not detained without local legal justification once their scheduled release time is reached.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request
evidence.why: It restricts the power of local jails to detain individuals on behalf of federal immigration authorities.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released
evidence.why: It removes the authority of local counties to decide whether their jails will honor federal immigration detainers.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request from federal immigration authorities.
evidence.why: It prohibits local jails from cooperating with federal immigration detainers by holding individuals past their release date.

evidence.quote: No county jail may hold a person beyond the time the person would otherwise be released solely on the basis of a detainer request from federal immigration authorities.
evidence.why: It protects immigrants from being held in local jails based solely on requests from federal immigration authorities.

analysis.answer: Current law leaves it up to each individual county to decide whether its jail will honor federal immigration detainer requests. This measure overrides that local discretion by imposing a statewide ban, prohibiting any county jail from holding an individual beyond their scheduled release time solely to fulfill such a detainer.

Counties that currently hold individuals on immigration detainers will be required to alter their release procedures to ensure individuals are freed once their local charges are resolved. In response, federal immigration authorities may need to conduct more apprehensions in the community or outside jails, rather than relying on local detention transfers.

The state government increases its authority over county jail operations by removing local policy discretion. Detained immigrants gain the assurance of timely release, while federal immigration enforcement loses a convenient mechanism for taking custody of individuals directly from local jails.
